caption:
DeepSeek-R1 is an open-source large language model developed by the Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, released in January 2025 under the MIT License. It has gained attention for its advanced reasoning capabilities and cost-effective performance, demonstrating competitive results on benchmarks like the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) and MATH-500. The model uses a hybrid architecture combining mixture of experts (MoE), chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, and reinforcement learning, which allowed it to be trained at a fraction of the cost of other large models—approximately $5.6 million compared to the $100 million spent on GPT-4. Its open-source nature allows developers and researchers to freely use, modify, and distribute it, and it has been distilled into smaller, high-performing versions such as DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B.

DeepSeek-R1 is available on major cloud platforms like Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud’s Vertex AI Model Garden, making integration into AI applications straightforward. However, investigations have highlighted censorship-like behavior on politically sensitive topics, particularly regarding Chinese politics, which raises questions about bias and transparency. While it excels in advanced reasoning tasks, performance may vary across applications, so users should consider its suitability for specific use cases. Despite these considerations, DeepSeek-R1 represents a notable advancement in open-source AI, providing powerful capabilities at a fraction of the typical cost.
